defaults.instructions:
ROLE
You are this business's WhatsApp assistant. You answer customer enquiries and product questions and represent the business professionally.

SCOPE
You help with:
- Products: features, specifications, variants, availability and usage
- General enquiries: business hours, location, how to order, delivery areas, payment methods and return policy
- The right next step: how to order, how to request a quotation, or reaching our team
You do not help with topics unrelated to the business or its products (general chat, news, coding, homework, opinions, politics, religion). Reply politely in one line and steer back, for example: "Sorry, I can only help with questions about our products and services. How can I help you with those?"

KNOWLEDGE
- Keep product names, model numbers and prices exactly as written in the business context.
- Never guess prices, stock, specifications, delivery dates, promotions or policies. If a detail is missing, say so and let our team confirm.
- Never promise discounts, free gifts or exceptions.

LANGUAGE
- Reply in the customer's language. If they mix languages, reply in the main language of their message.
- If you cannot reply in their language, use the default language named in the business context, otherwise English.

STYLE
- Professional, polite and friendly; no slang. At most one emoji, and only where it fits.
- One to three short sentences. Use a short list only for options or specifications.
- Answer first: no long greetings and no repeating the question back.
- Ask at most one clarifying question when needed (for example which model, size or area).
- WhatsApp formatting only: *bold* for key details and plain line breaks. No headings, tables or links you were not given.
defaults.handoffRules:
- The customer is upset or makes a complaint
- The customer asks for a refund, return, exchange or warranty claim
- The customer asks about an existing order, delivery or payment
- The customer wants a bulk or custom order, or a quotation
- The customer wants to negotiate the price or asks for a discount

mockApi.removeBody: EzyChat stops receiving and sending for this number and removes its webhook. The number stays on the Business API in your Meta account. Its chats stay, read only, for admins.

webhook.offTitle: Turn on Phone access to receive messages
webhook.offBody: Meta delivers messages to a public https address. Turn on Phone access (Cloudflare) and EzyChat registers that address with Meta for you. Until then customers' messages wait at Meta (up to 7 days).
webhook.quickNote: Registered with Meta automatically. A Quick Tunnel gets a new address when it restarts; EzyChat registers the new one at once.
webhook.namedNote: Registered with Meta automatically on your own address.
webhook.failBody: Meta reports delivery errors for this address. Check that Phone access is running; EzyChat registers the address again and Meta retries for up to 7 days.

mockApi.tunnelNoteTitle: Business API messages arrive through Phone access
mockApi.tunnelNoteBody: Keep Phone access running for {{names}}: Meta delivers its messages to this address. EzyChat registers the address with Meta whenever it changes.
mockApi.switchToApi1: Register this same number on the WhatsApp Business API in your Meta app first. Meta then removes it from the WhatsApp app on the phone.
mockApi.switchToApi2: EzyChat unlinks the phone and connects the number through Meta. The inbox, its chats, notes, tags and assignments stay as they are.
mockApi.switchToApi3: After the move, the 24-hour reply window and templates apply to this inbox.
mockApi.switchedToApi: The inbox now uses the Business API. Its chats stay.
mockApi.switchToPhone: Switch back to the WhatsApp app (QR)
mockApi.switchToPhoneBody: EzyChat removes the webhook and stops using the Business API for this number. Remove the number from the Business API in Meta, then scan the QR code with the phone. The chats stay in this inbox.
mockApi.switchToPhoneConfirm: Switch and show the QR code
mockApi.switchedToPhone: Switched. Scan the QR code with the phone.
mockApi.errorOtherNumber: This phone number ID belongs to another number. This inbox is {{number}}: its chats stay together only with the same number.

mockSuggest.title: Reply suggestions
mockSuggest.description: Teammates press Suggest reply in a chat to get 2 AI drafts, and the AI completes the sentence they type. The AI never sends a message.
mockSuggest.cost: Each suggestion and each completion is one request to your AI provider, which may charge for it.
mockSuggest.noConnection: Connect an AI provider above to use reply suggestions.
mockSuggest.upgraded: New: reply suggestions. They are off after the update so that nothing new costs money without your choice.

mockPhrases.title: Phrase list
mockPhrases.description: Instant grey text from phrases your team uses. The AI builds the list in the background from your business context, the AI instructions and the team's sent replies, and keeps it up to date.
mockPhrases.off: Reply suggestions are off, so the phrase list does not update and is not used.
mockPhrases.building: Building the phrase list. The AI reads your business context and the team's replies…
mockPhrases.empty: No phrase list yet. It builds by itself a few minutes after the app starts, or press Build now.
mockPhrases.error: The phrase list could not be built. The AI did not answer. Try again later.
mockPhrases.next: Next update after {{count}} more team replies, or when the business context changes.
mockPhrases.calls: AI calls for the list today: {{used}} of at most {{limit}}.
mockPhrases.privacy: The list stays in this app. Customer names and phone numbers are removed. Teammates moving a phrase up with Tab is counted here only.
mockPhrases.listDescription: Phrases show as grey text when a teammate's last words match. Most used first. Facts (prices, hours) are checked against the business context.
mockPhrases.fact: Fact checked against the business context
mockPhrases.modelFastHint: Suggest reply in about 1–2 s and grey text while you type. {{model}} is the fast model of this connection.
mockPhrases.modelSlowHint: A larger model writes slower: grey text often comes too late to help, and each request may cost more.

mockCalendar.title: Google Calendar
mockCalendar.description: Let your AI agent check free times and book appointments in your Google Calendar. No link to paste: sign in with Google.
mockCalendar.what1: The AI offers only times that are free in the calendar you choose.
mockCalendar.what2: It books only after the customer confirms a time, and you can keep booking off.
mockCalendar.what3: Your team sees every booking in the chat.

mockCalendar.unavailableBody: EzyChat tries again on its own. Meanwhile the AI hands booking chats to your team.
mockCalendar.perAgent: Choose the calendar and booking hours for each AI agent in Settings.
mockCalendar.disconnectBody: The AI stops checking and booking times at once. Events already in your calendar stay. Booking settings are kept for when you connect again.
mockCalendar.scope1: See your calendars and when you are busy
mockCalendar.scope2: Add and change events in your calendars
mockCalendar.agentDescription: {{name}} can check free times and book appointments in Google Calendar.
mockCalendar.agentNotConnected: Connect Google Calendar first. It takes one sign-in with Google.
mockCalendar.agentPausedBody: Until it works again, {{name}} hands booking chats to your team.
mockCalendar.calendarHint: Bookings go into this calendar, and only its busy times count.
mockCalendar.checkFreeHint: The AI may read when this calendar is busy and offer free times.
mockCalendar.bookHint: The AI adds an event after the customer confirms a time. Off: the AI offers times and your team books.
mockCalendar.bookNeedsFree: Turn on Check free times first.
mockCalendar.eventTitleHint: The customer's name is added, e.g. "Table booking · Mei Ying".
mockCalendar.hoursHint: Times outside these hours, and times already busy in the calendar, are never offered.
mockCalendar.rule1: The AI books only after the customer confirms one time in their own words.
mockCalendar.rule2: EzyChat checks the time is still free just before it books.

google-calendar.name: Google Calendar
google-calendar.short: Check free times and book appointments.
google-calendar.long: Your AI agent offers free times from your Google Calendar and, if you allow it, books the time the customer confirms. Sign in with Google: no link to paste.

tools.checkFreeHint: Reads when the chosen calendar is busy.
tools.bookHint: Adds an event after the customer confirms a time.

google-calendar.privacy: EzyChat reads busy times of the calendar you choose and writes only the events it books: title, and the customer’s name, phone and email. No chat text goes to Google. The sign-in is stored encrypted on this computer.

google-sheets.name: Google Sheets
google-sheets.short: Read prices or stock from a sheet; add new leads.

mockGrammar.title: Fix English
mockGrammar.description: While a teammate types an English reply, spelling mistakes are underlined at once and grammar mistakes after a short pause. One tap fixes them; nothing is changed or sent without the teammate.
mockGrammar.cost: Spelling is checked on this device with a built-in British English dictionary (about 0.2 MB, loaded once): free, no AI. Grammar is one short AI request after each pause in typing (the fast model). Malay and Chinese messages are not checked.
mockGrammar.rules: It fixes spelling and grammar only. Numbers, prices, names, links and order numbers are never changed, and the teammate's tone stays (lah, ya).
mockGrammar.noConnection: No AI connection: only spelling is checked. Connect AI above to check grammar too.
mockGrammar.upgraded: New: Fix English is off after the update. Switch it on to help the team write correct English.
mockGrammar.wordsHint: Never underlined: product, place and customer words that the dictionary does not know. Words from your Business context are added by themselves; teammates add more from the underline.

mockResolution.onHint: After an answer, {{name}} asks whether it answers the question and closes the chat when the customer clearly says yes.
